messages:
Liam Carter: Quick thread 1: want to propose an ownership TTL model and a compact handoff template for postmortem follow-ups. TL;DR: short leases on ownership + explicit handoff steps = fewer stalled remediation cards.

Ana Morales: sounds useful. what does TTL mean here?

Liam Carter: TTL = time-to-live for an assigned remediation. default 7 days for P1	, 14 days for P2. if owner doesn't update in 48h 1 escalate to on-call lead. goal is to avoid month+ open followups.

Priya Nair: love the escalation thresholds. can we make owners opt-in to a 72h "deep-dive" buffer if the work requires design time?

Liam Carter: yes, optional buffer with explicit justification in the ticket. but owner must still post an interim update every 48h.

Theo Zhang: propose a minimal handoff message that must be added when ownership changes. it should live in the issue/epic description. example snippet below.

Theo Zhang: ```yaml
handoff:
  from: "@previous_owner"
  to: "@new_owner"
  date: "2025-06-12T15:00Z"
  summary: "short list of remaining steps (3 bullets max)"
  blockers: "any known blockers or 'none'"
  expected_ttl_days: 7
```

Ana Morales: can we also require a "success metric" line so we know how to mark the remediation done?

Liam Carter: absolutely. add `success_metric` field to that snippet.

Priya Nair: aside from TTL, we should track "owner churn" - if a followup changes owners more than twice, flag it for process review and ask the original IC for context.

pagerbot: Followup PROJ-3344 created for incident 1813456789. Owner: Liam Carter. TTL: 7d. Escalation in 48h if no update.

Theo Zhang: on comms cadence: incident thread updates should stick to a micro-template: 1) what changed, 2) next action, 3) ETA. keep under 3 bullets. for followups, weekly status is fine unless TTL is active.

Ana Morales: what about rotation for ICs? we currently rotate 1 week, maybe move to 2 weeks to improve continuity.

Priya Nair: 2 weeks makes sense for complex incidents. but create a quick IC playbook card with a 5-min checklist for handing off to make rotation cheaper.

Liam Carter: included below a short IC handoff checklist to add to the runbook. copy/paste into the incident bot when handing off.

Liam Carter: ```
IC Handoff Checklist:
- State current severity & impact numbers
- List open mitigations + owners
- Link to followup epic(s)
- Note any required approvals / deployment windows
- Next expected update time
```

Theo Zhang: operational suggestion: the followup epic should have 3 visible fields: owner, ttl_days, success_metric. this makes dashboards easier to query.

Ana Morales: queries we want in the weekly SRE digest: top 10 open followups by age, followups with owner churn >1, recurrence-radar hits (if any).

Priya Nair: for recurrence detection: we can run a lightweight similarity check using: normalized stack frames, error fingerprint + time-of-day clustering. if similarity > 0.8, mark as candidate. include candidate reason in the epic.

pagerbot: Recurrence check scheduled for incident 1813456789: candidate match found -> INCIDENT-201 (score 0.83). Created followup PROJ-3345.

Liam Carter: next practical steps I propose: (1) add YAML handoff snippet to runbook (Liam) - PR in 48h; (2) add TTL fields to followup epic template and wire pagerbot to set escalation timers (Theo) - spike in 7d; (3) add owner-churn alert in weekly digest (Ana) - add to digest next week; (4) run two-week trial on upcoming P1s (Priya) - start this sprint.

Theo Zhang: I'll prototype pagerbot behavior: set TTL expiry timer, post reminder at 48h, escalate to oncall-leads if no updates, and annotate owner-churn when assignment count >2.

Ana Morales: also please make the bot pin the followup epic link in the original incident thread and add a single-line summary card. small UX wins help adoption.

Priya Nair: agreed. if everyone is +1, i'll coordinate the trial and collect metrics: closure rate within TTL, owner churn count, recurrence candidates surfaced.

Liam Carter: all +1 from me. thanks. we'll iterate after the trial.

pagerbot: Reminder: 48h TTL check scheduled for PROJ-3344 (owner: Liam Carter).
